catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries one scalar MSO5000 automatic measurement scoped to an analog source: cap.sensing.read.v1 binds only the resource kinds sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque, not instrument, and cap.measure.spectrum.v1 is a spectrum sweep. The action wraps the clone's MEASure:ITEM? query and returns one value.

No catalogue class starts continuous acquisition on an instrument: cap.process.run.v1 is a process recipe, cap.device.self_test.v1 is a self-test and cap.device.calibrate.v1 is a calibration. The action calls the native RUN command and returns the run state read back with trigger_status.

cap.device.configure.v1 fits these channel-1 fields, but one capability may be bound only once and the combined standard configure binding (ten writes) produced a 2492-byte MCP tool, above the 2048-byte bound. Splitting the channel display, coupling, probe ratio and bandwidth filter into this action keeps both tools under the bound. The action writes through the native set_channel, which is the same upstream call the configure fields use.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a ScpiDriver (family-config, family scpi), but the upstream interface is the object pymso5000.scope:Scope with typed methods and read-back outcomes rather than a table of fixed command lines (scope.py:565-603, 619-734, 738-793); every channel command is assembled with a channel number, so this is a direct Driver over the upstream class with native.py, as driver-authoring.md 'Choosing the shape' requires. The repo is a VISA SCPI client for Rigol MSO5000 series oscilloscopes; this package serves analog channel 1 and the shared acquisition/timebase state. NOT COVERED: waveform arrays (the standard cannot carry the large sample array yet); the vertical settings of channels 2 to 4 (the measurement action can name any analog channel as its source, but their settings are not read or set); the logic analyzer, the built-in generator, the trigger subsystem (only RUN/STOP and the run-state read are served), decode, the front panel and the setup blob. The four numeric span/position writes (channel1_scale_per_div, channel1_offset, timebase_scale_s_per_div, timebase_offset_s) are Limit.operator_required: the programming guide states their ranges only per probe ratio, vertical scale, model or timebase mode, and the clone only refuses a non-positive span or a non-finite position; site-limits.example.json shows one narrowing overlay, and without it those four writes are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The channel-1 display, coupling, probe ratio and bandwidth filter are x-cap.mabl.scope_channel_input.v1 rather than fields of cap.device.configure.v1 because one standard configure binding with all ten writes made the MCP tool 2492 bytes (limit 2048); the standard binding keeps acquisition_type, memory_depth, channel1_scale_per_div, channel1_offset, timebase_scale_s_per_div and timebase_offset_s. The fake is an in-memory stand-in with placeholder values (each marked # placeholder), not a recording: the clone has no simulator for Scope and no hardware was available, so the card's preferred transcript could not be recorded. The fake implements only names that exist on Scope (G7). The measurement action uses the documented Scope.execute escape hatch to issue MEASure:ITEM?; it returns only a scalar value, not a unit or the on-screen measurement list. driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null: the package is model-authored and unreviewed, checked on the fake backend only, and nothing in it ran on hardware. The loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package at R2 and R3 only; this package is R1 and does not claim that guard. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
